entities.name: Archaic Period
entities.label: Timeframe
entities.summary: The Archaic Period, spanning approximately 800 BCE to 480 BCE, marks a transformative epoch in ancient Greek history, laying the essential groundwork for the subsequent Classical era. This timeframe witnessed the emergence and consolidation of the polis, or city-state, as the dominant political and social unit, fundamentally reshaping Hellenic identity and governance. It was an age of profound cultural and societal restructuring, moving beyond the 'Dark Ages' into a period of renewed literacy, artistic expression, and interregional connectivity, crucial for the development of Western civilization.
